meta.name: MDF Boards
meta.definition: Medium-density fibreboard (MDF) is an engineered wood panel made by breaking down hardwood or softwood residuals into fine wood fibres, blending them with resin and wax, and forming panels under high heat and pressure. Denser and smoother than plywood, it is the default substrate for modern furniture, laminates, doors and interior fit-outs.

summary.headline: India's MDF market is riding a structural shift from plywood to engineered panels — growing double digits on furniture demand, housing and import substitution.
key_takeaways: MDF is steadily replacing plywood in furniture and interiors, expanding ~13% a year.
Domestic capacity has nearly doubled since 2020; plant utilisation is the key margin swing.
Anti-dumping duties have shielded local makers from cheap Southeast Asian imports.
Greenpanel and Action Tesa lead a market consolidating around large, integrated plants.
Timber, resin and methanol costs drive input volatility and thin the margin cushion.
summary.report_markdown:
## What MDF is
Medium-density fibreboard is an **engineered wood panel** made from wood fibre, resin and wax pressed into smooth, uniform boards. Its flat surface takes lamination, paint and veneer far better than plywood, which is why it has become the default material for **modular furniture, wardrobes, doors and interior fit-outs**.

## Market size & growth
The Indian MDF market is estimated at roughly **₹5,800 crore in 2025**, up from about ₹3,000 crore in 2020 — a five-year CAGR in the low-teens. Growth is driven less by cyclical construction and more by a **structural substitution of plywood by MDF** as furniture manufacturing formalises.

## Demand drivers
- **Plywood-to-MDF shift** as furniture makers value a consistent, machinable surface.
- **Modular kitchens and ready-to-assemble (RTA) furniture**, where MDF is the standard core.
- **Housing completions and renovation cycles** lifting panel consumption.
- **Pre-lamination and value-add** improving realisations per board.

## Competitive landscape
The market is consolidating around a handful of large, integrated players. **Greenpanel** is the largest MDF-focused manufacturer, followed by the unlisted **Action Tesa**, with **Century Plyboards, Rushil Décor and Greenply** building scale. Regional mills and imports make up the long tail.

## Supply, capacity & trade
A wave of new large-format lines has **roughly doubled installed capacity since 2020**. As a result, **utilisation** — not headline demand — is the swing factor for pricing and margins. **Anti-dumping duties** on imports from Thailand, Vietnam, Indonesia and Malaysia have curbed the flow of cheap panels and supported domestic realisations.

## Margins & economics
Manufacturer EBITDA margins run in the **mid-teens** at healthy utilisation, thinning quickly when plants run below ~70%. Dealer margins sit around **8–14%**, with pre-laminated board earning more than plain MDF.

## Risks to watch
- Import resurgence if duty cover lapses or the rupee strengthens.
- Oversupply and price wars as new capacity ramps.
- Volatile timber, resin and methanol input costs.
- MDF's moisture sensitivity in wet-area applications versus plywood.

## Outlook
The demand story is **structural rather than cyclical**, but the next two years hinge on how quickly new capacity is absorbed. Players with scale, pre-lamination mix and export access are best placed to defend margins.
